policy_excerpts.text:
# Bleep blorp these are the `trimesh` AI preferences

Contributions are welcome, and AI is obviously a great tool! However there are a few notes:

- We're trying to keep every line human-read and human-run at least once, so the larger the diff the less likely a PR is to be merged.
- Please only open one PR at a time.
- Please keep AI text in written issues and PR bodies to 50 words or less.
- API changes, dependency additions, "full algorithm rewrites" without prior discussion are pretty unlikely to be merged.
- Please read the `contributing.md` guide for instructions on surgical fixes with maximal test coverage.

name: PR Policy

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, reopened]

permissions:
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  one-open-pr-per-author:
    name: One Open PR Per Author
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Enforce one open PR per author
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
        run: |
          # collaborators are exempt — gh exits 0 on 204, nonzero on 404
          gh api "repos/$GH_REPO/collaborators/$AUTHOR" --silent 2>/dev/null && exit 0
          # --author filters server-side; gh reads the repo from $GH_REPO
          others=$(gh pr list --state open --author "$AUTHOR" \
            --json number --jq "[.[] | select(.number != $PR) | \"#\(.number)\"] | join(\", \")")
          [ -z "$others" ] && exit 0
          gh pr close "$PR" --comment "Thanks for the contribution! This repository limits contributors to **one open pull request at a time**.

          You already have an open PR ($others), so this one is being closed automatically. Please continue in that PR, or close it and reopen this when ready."

### Pull Request Limits and Escalation

vLLM uses GitHub's [pull request limit](https://github.blog/open-source/maintainers/how-pull-request-limits-are-cutting-down-the-noise/)
for contributors without write access. The current cap is 6 open PRs. If this
blocks well-intentioned critical work, contact a committer to request bypass
list access.

Community contributors can have only one open pull request at a time in this repository. Before opening a PR on the user's behalf, check whether they already have one open (`gh pr list --author @me`); if so, tell them instead of opening another.

### Using AI assistants to contribute

You may use AI assistants or agents to help you implement a contribution. Please use them wisely:

- **Review and understand** all generated code before submitting. You are responsible for the contribution.
- **Run tests and checks** locally (e.g. `hatch run test:unit`, `hatch run fmt`) so your PR meets our quality bar.
- **If your PR was fully AI-generated**, add a short disclaimer in the PR description, for example: *"This PR was
  fully generated with an AI assistant. I have reviewed the changes and run the relevant tests."*

This helps maintainers and keeps the project ready for both human and AI contributors.

name: First-time contributor PR limit

# Keep the review queue manageable: a first-time contributor may have at most
# one open pull request in this repository until that PR has been approved.
#
# A contributor counts as first-time while they have neither a merged PR nor a
# PR with an approving review in this repository. For such an author, every
# open PR except their oldest one is closed with an explanatory comment. Once
# the first PR is approved (or merged), the limit no longer applies.
#
# Team members and bots are exempt. author_association is unreliable for this
# (private org members appear as CONTRIBUTOR/NONE in the payload), so the
# effective repository permission is checked as a fallback. Maintainers can
# opt a PR out by adding the `skip-pr-limit` label before reopening it.
#
# Uses pull_request_target so it can act on fork PRs; this is safe because the
# workflow never checks out or executes PR code.

name: PR flood guard

# Ask community contributors to slow down when review capacity is the
# bottleneck. On every newly opened PR from outside the org, warn if:
#  - another open PR already targets the same linked issue (duplicate), or
#  - the author already has more than two PRs open in this repository.
#
# Uses pull_request_target so it can comment on fork PRs; this is safe because
# the workflow never checks out or executes PR code.

### Working with AI

AI tools are welcome. Check their output as you would your own and describe the actual
human contribution and its effect: steering, diagnosis, design decisions, edits, review,
or supervision. Arranging another model's review is distinct from personally verifying
the result; credit AI-generated findings and tests to the AI. Merely requesting the task
or directing an agent to follow reviews can mean zero substantive human technical
contribution. The PR template asks for this distinction, not a percentage or a chat transcript.

Every agent-authored GitHub PR description, issue, comment, and review on a user's behalf
ends with `Posted on behalf of @<github-handle> by <Agent> (<actual model>).` Use the actual
handle, agent, and model rather than a generic generated-by footer.

- **Say so in the PR.** If an AI assistant wrote or substantially helped with the change,
  state that in the PR description, and which tool, so the reviewer knows what to look for. You,
  the human, remain responsible for what you submit and should have read the diff.
- **Sign the commits.** An AI-assisted commit ends with a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming the
  tool and model, as Claude Code does by default, and the PR description ends with the tool's
  attribution line. The repository squash-merges, so the PR description is what survives; keep
  the disclosure there as well as in the commits.

## AI-assisted contributions

AI coding assistants are welcome, but please say so in the PR description (and which tool),
so the reviewer knows what to look for. Also keep the `Co-Authored-By:` trailer on the commits
(most tools add it), since the repository squash-merges and the PR description is what is kept.
You remain responsible for what you submit, so read
the diff yourself and run the tests before asking for review.

- **Please disclose significant AI assistance.** If you used AI tools (e.g., Copilot, Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT) to generate a substantial portion of your code or text, let us know in your PR description. Transparency helps us review your changes more effectively.
- **Bring your judgment to every contribution (The Human-in-the-Loop).** You are responsible for everything you submit and should understand the changes you are proposing. Before inviting review, please read and refine AI-assisted work. Call out any uncertainty so reviewers know where their input would help. If you cannot explain a change or how it fits LeRobot's broader architecture, take the time to learn and test it before submitting.
- **Help readers find what matters.** You are welcome to use AI to help draft issues or PR descriptions, but please review and edit them carefully before posting. Keeping the useful reasoning while removing repetition, filler, and unnecessary length helps maintainers respond more effectively.

5. **Disclose significant AI assistance.** If AI generated a substantial part of your code or text, briefly describe what it helped with in the PR description. Routine autocomplete does not need disclosure. Include any unresolved uncertainty or limitations that reviewers should know about.

### AI-assisted contributions

AI-assisted contributions are welcome. The submitting contributor is responsible
for understanding the change, reviewing the complete diff, verifying the PR
description and reported validation results, and addressing review feedback.
Clearly distinguish verified behavior from assumptions and untested claims.

Before opening a PR or changing its title, an agent should show the exact
proposed title and ask the contributor to confirm or replace it. A title supplied
by the contributor, or explicit permission to choose the title without asking,
satisfies this step. Do not repeat confirmation when the title is unchanged.
The [submission skill](.agents/skills/tilelang-submit-pr/SKILL.md#confirm-the-pr-title)
describes this interaction.

You may optionally include `AI assistance: <tool name>` in the PR description.
Disclosing the tool is not a requirement for review or merging. The repository's
submission skill offers this choice when preparing a new PR and adds the field
only when the contributor opts in.
